title: Demonstration of Flying-Focus-Enhanced Relativistic Thomson Scattering
abstract: We report the experimental demonstration of a spatiotemporally engineered "flying-focus" laser pulse for enhanced X-ray generation via relativistic Thomson scattering. By combining longitudinal chromatic aberration, angular dispersion, and group delay dispersion, we create a relativistically intense laser pulse whose focal point propagates with an independently tunable velocity vector, enabling control of both its speed and propagation angle. Precise tuning of the focal-point trajectory is used to match the motion of a near-counterpropagating ultrarelativistic electron bunch generated by a laser wakefield accelerator. This spatiotemporal velocity matching extends the interaction length while mitigating nonlinear scattering effects, resulting in an enhanced X-ray yield. Simulations indicate that this approach can increase the spectral density and brightness of Thomson-scattered X-ray beams by orders of magnitude relative to equivalent focusing without spatiotemporal control. The technique provides a new degree of freedom for high-intensity laser-matter interactions, allowing dynamic intensity structures with programmable two-dimensional motion and opening a route to enhanced laser-particle interactions and next-generation ultrabright radiation sources.
